title: State Pension uprating analysis 2026
figure_text: In-year AME savings of the adjusted Triple Lock relative to the Triple Lock: -£15 billion in 2039 to 2040 (nominal; -£11 billion in 2025 to 2026 prices)
comparison: Burnham plan vs triple lock, State Pension spending, 2039-40, nominal
note: DWP runs one deterministic uprating path (not stated) through Pensim3, a dynamic population model, for Great Britain, rounded to £1bn. Ours is the expected gross saving over calibrated paths, each a full run on the Enhanced FRS for the UK, with survey ages held fixed.

title: Long-term economic determinants, March 2026 EFO
figure_text: 'Triple lock': Average earnings growth plus 0.6 percentage points (long-term growth rate assumption)
comparison: Long-run triple-lock rise above earnings growth, a year (decimal)
note: The OBR's premium is an assumption for its long-term projections. Ours is the expected triple-lock rise less May-July earnings growth for the April 2034-2039 rises (inputs of 2033-2038) under the primary distribution: rule arithmetic, not a fiscal figure.

title: Fiscal risks and sustainability - July 2025
figure_text: "the triple lock is expected to have cost £15.5 billion annually by 2029-30, around three times higher than initial expectations" (vs the original 2012 estimate of £5.2bn)
comparison: Triple lock vs earnings uprating since 2012; annual cost in 2029-30 of the cumulative ratchet
note: OBR compares the triple lock with earnings uprating since 2012, in 2029-30. Ours is the gross saving in 2026-27 had the Burnham plan, which keeps the higher of CPI and 2.5% as a floor, started in April 2012.

title: What a ratchet! (Curtice and Clegg)
figure_text: The State Pension bill is £12.6bn higher than under a smoothed earnings link since 2012, or about £9bn net of tax and means-tested benefit interactions
comparison: Triple lock vs smoothed earnings link since 2012, cumulative ratchet, net
note: RF compares with a smoothed earnings link; ours is the net saving in 2026-27 had the Burnham plan (which keeps a CPI and 2.5% floor) started in April 2012.

title: Fiscal risks and sustainability - July 2026
figure_text: In the baseline, state pension spending rises from 5% to around 9% of GDP over the 50-year projection, driven by ageing and triple-lock uprating; under earnings uprating it reaches around 7% of GDP
comparison: Triple lock vs earnings uprating over 50 years, with volatility calibrated to history, % of GDP
note: A 50-year horizon in % of GDP with ageing; ours is in £bn for 2039-40, with survey ages held fixed. Same direction: once CPI and earnings vary, the ratchet costs far more than on a central path (see central.run.saving_bn).
